extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes the MacArthur Foundation's purpose, program priorities, and the selection/eligibility principles used for flagship programs (e.g., MacArthur Fellows, 100&Change, targeted initiatives such as the Just Home Project).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation stated purpose / alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation's stated purpose is to support "creative people, effective institutions, and influential networks building a more just, verdant, and peaceful world".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals and activities that align with advancing justice, environmental sustainability (verdant), peacebuilding, and strengthening creative individuals, institutions, or networks are consistent with the foundation's mission and more likely to fit its portfolio priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: mitigating climate change
rubrics_metrics.description: MacArthur's grant-making priorities include mitigating climate change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation gives priority to work addressing climate change; proposals that clearly target climate mitigation or adaptation and demonstrate potential impact align with this priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: reducing jail populations
rubrics_metrics.description: MacArthur's grant-making priorities include reducing jail populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiatives that propose strategies to decrease incarceration rates or address drivers of jail populations (e.g., alternatives to incarceration, reentry services, policy reform) align with this priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: decreasing nuclear threats
rubrics_metrics.description: MacArthur's grant-making priorities include decreasing nuclear threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs or research aimed at reducing nuclear risk, policy change, arms control, or related advocacy fit this listed priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: supporting nonprofit journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: MacArthur's grant-making priorities include supporting nonprofit journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants that strengthen nonprofit news organizations, investigative journalism, or sustainable journalism models align with this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority: funding local needs in Chicago
rubrics_metrics.description: MacArthur's grant-making priorities include funding local needs in its hometown of Chicago.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects serving Chicago communities, addressing local problems, or partnering with Chicago-based organizations align with this geographic/local priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: MacArthur Fellows selection criterion — originality and promise
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows are individuals who "show exceptional merit and promise for continued and enhanced creative work"; the fellowship is "not a reward for past accomplishment, but an investment in a person's originality and potential."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection emphasizes demonstrated originality and future potential rather than solely past achievements. Proposals (or nominations) should highlight ongoing creative trajectory and capacity for further significant work.

rubrics_metrics.name: MacArthur Fellows process requirement — nomination and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: No one can apply for the program; nominators are invited and serve confidentially and anonymously for a limited time; candidates are reviewed by a confidential selection committee whose recommendations go to the foundation's board for final approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Fellows program is nomination-only and highly confidential; eligibility/selection depends on being identified by invited nominators and evaluated by committee—not on open application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: 100&Change selection criterion — real progress on a critical problem
rubrics_metrics.description: For 100&Change the foundation requested "proposals promising real progress toward solving a critical problem of our time in any field or any location."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The competition sought a single proposal capable of delivering measurable, substantial progress on a major societal problem. Submissions were expected to demonstrate plausibility of real-world impact, scalability, and clear metrics of success; the program awards one $100 million grant approximately every three years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for large, transformative grants ('Big Bets')
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation has undertaken a strategic shift toward 'Big Bets'—making larger, targeted investments intended to drive major impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MacArthur shows a strategic appetite for fewer, larger investments designed to produce substantial, systemic change. Projects proposing transformative, high-impact interventions are consistent with this approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted initiative design requirement — community-driven partnerships (example: Just Home Project)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Just Home Project provides grant funding to selected communities to create unique plans that "bring together government officials, non-profit partners, and impacted communities members to develop innovative approaches" to break links between housing instability and jail incarceration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiatives funded under targeted projects emphasize local community partnership, cross-sector collaboration (government + non-profits + affected community members), context-specific planning, and technical assistance. Funded proposals should demonstrate collaborative design and local engagement.
